newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fire kills 15 in HK karaoke bar, arson suspected.
newsitem.headline: Fire kills 15 in HK karaoke bar, arson suspected.

text.p: Fifteen people burned to death on Saturday when a fire believed to have been set by an arsonist gutted a karaoke night club in Hong Kong in the territory's second major fire tragedy in as many months.
Most of the casualties were young people. Thirteen survivors were taken to hospital and two were listed in critical condition, hospital sources said.
A police spokesman said the blaze appeared to have been started deliberately because it had flared up on a first-floor staircase, spreading rapidly to the higher floors.
The dead included five men and 10 women.
The blaze raced through the Top One karaoke bar in the Tsimshatsui nightlife district of Hong Kong's Kowloon Peninsula shortly around 4 a.m. (2000 GMT)
Survivors fled the building down firemen's ladders as the blaze raced from the first floor to the second and third. It took firefighters less than an hour and half to extinguish the fire.
Police cordoned off the street around the bar and sent in arson detectives to scour the wreckage for clues.
Governor Chris Patten went to the scene, offered his sympathies to the victims and their families, and visited the survivors in hospital.
Patten vowed every effort would be made to find the cause of the fire, calling it "another dreadful incident."
"I'd like to thank the fire service for reacting so rapidly to this incident, surrounding which, as you know already, there are certainly suspicious circumstances," Patten told reporters.
"I'd like to offer my condolences to the families of the young victims, their suffering today is, for all of us who are parents I'm sure, literally unimaginable," Patten said.

It was the second major fire tragedy in Hong Kong in as many months. In late November 40 people were killed in Hong Kong's worst building blaze on record when fire gutted a commercial block in Kowloon's "golden mile" Nathan Road shopping district.
That blaze triggered a public outcry demanding more stringent fire safety standards for Hong Kong's residential and office buildings.
Earlier this month legislators endorsed a motion urging a review of building management, noting that the building hit by the November fire lacked proper firefighting devices.
